text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/01/02 - Essay - 01
People share a meal and conversation.
Pexels · 9220890
Around the table
The decision to share a meal may appear ordinary, yet it exposes a recurring tension between arrangements that make life manageable and
experiences that resist being prescribed. A defensible approach combines proportionate preparation with a willingness to reconsider whose
interests a plan serves.
Preparation has value because a simple plan leaves time for conversation. In the present case, we prepare the vegetables before our guests
arrive. Such an intervention is modest, but that modesty is its strength: it removes a foreseeable obstacle without claiming to determine the
entire experience. Structure is useful to the extent that it releases attention rather than consuming it.
That argument requires a qualification, however: sharing the work helps everyone feel included. For instance, each guest brings one dish and
helps clear the table. An arrangement that appears efficient from one standpoint may impose costs elsewhere. Listening to those affected is
therefore not an optional gesture of goodwill; it supplies information without which the plan cannot be adequately evaluated.
The resulting principle is one of proportion. Preparation deserves support when it clarifies responsibilities and protects time, while
responsiveness prevents it from hardening into an end in itself. To judge the experience well is to examine both what the arrangement
enables and what it may inadvertently exclude.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each body
paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Write about an attempt to share a meal that did not go as planned. Explain two lessons, each supported by a specific incident. Use four short
paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss a simple plan
leaves time for conversation with an example; discuss sharing the work helps everyone feel included with a different example; conclude by
connecting the two points.)
